executive_summary: The shop's resilience is compromised by three services whose latency spikes cascade to every major user journey, creating a critical wide-blast-radius risk. Additionally, the cart, flagd, and valkey-cart services act as single points of failure: their crashes isolate the cart journey, exposing a lack of redundancy. Recovery times are within the normal floor, so the primary focus should be on reducing cross-service latency impact and adding failover or isolation for the identified single-point services.

weaknesses.title: Wide blast radius - frontend latency
weaknesses.explanation: A 100 ms delay on the frontend triggers a watchdog breach, causing all four core journeys (cart, checkout, home, product) to exceed latency SLOs, yielding impact 1.00 and breadth 1.00. The fault spreads across the entire user experience.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-141542-f9bb delay 100ms on frontend: impact 1.00 breadth 1.00, degraded cart,checkout,home,product

fix.fix_title: Add timeout, retry and circuit breaker to frontend calls
fix.steps: Update the frontend entry code to wrap all outbound HTTP calls with a 200ms timeout. On timeout, automatically retry up to 2 times with exponential backoff (50ms, 100ms). Integrate a circuit-breaker library that opens after 3 consecutive failures and serves cached static responses for 30s before half-opening. Deploy the updated image and run smoke tests.
fix.expected_effect: Transient 100ms delays no longer trigger the watchdog breach; journeys stay within the 800ms SLO by falling back to cached data.

weaknesses.title: Wide blast radius - astronomy-db latency
weaknesses.explanation: Injecting 300 ms latency into astronomy-db degrades every major journey, pushing cart and checkout p95 latencies far beyond the 800 ms threshold, with impact 1.00 and breadth 1.00.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-143142-3011 delay 300ms on astronomy-db: impact 1.00 breadth 1.00, degraded cart,checkout,home,product

fix.steps: Deploy a Redis container as a read-through cache. Modify the astronomy-db client library to check Redis first; on miss, query the DB and populate the cache with a 120s TTL. Configure the service to use the cache endpoint. Verify cache hit rate improves latency under injected delays.
fix.expected_effect: Read queries bypass the delayed DB, keeping cart and checkout p95 latencies under the threshold despite 300ms DB latency.

weaknesses.title: Wide blast radius - product-catalog latency
weaknesses.explanation: A 300 ms delay on product-catalog causes product and cart latency breaches, degrading all core journeys with full impact and breadth, indicating a systemic dependency on this service.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-164224-dcfe delay 300ms on product-catalog: impact 1.00 breadth 1.00, degraded cart,checkout,home,product

fix.steps: Add an in-memory LRU cache in the product-catalog client within the frontend service. Cache the full catalog payload for 60s. On each request, serve from cache if present; otherwise fetch from product-catalog with a 200ms timeout and fallback to stale cache on timeout. Deploy updated frontend image.
fix.expected_effect: A 300ms product-catalog delay is masked by cached data, preventing journey-wide latency breaches.

weaknesses.title: Single point of failure - cart service crash
weaknesses.explanation: Crashing the cart service aborts the cart journey entirely (breadth 0.25) while other journeys remain unaffected, showing the cart service is a single point of failure for order flow.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-142250-d200 crash on cart: impact 1.00 breadth 0.25, degraded cart only

fix.fix_title: Enable restart policy and memory limit for cart service
fix.steps: Create a compose override that sets restart: unless-stopped and limits memory to 512M for the cart container. Apply the override and redeploy the cart service. Verify the container restarts automatically after a crash and stays within the memory budget.
fix.expected_effect: Cart crashes are automatically recovered, eliminating the single point of failure for the cart journey.

weaknesses.title: Single point of failure - flagd & valkey-cart crashes
weaknesses.explanation: Crashes of flagd and valkey-cart each abort the cart journey alone (breadth 0.25), revealing that these auxiliary services are critical single points for cart functionality.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-141616-6842 crash on flagd and exp-104221-fd4f crash on valkey-cart: impact 1.00 breadth 0.25, degraded cart only

fix.fix_title: Add redundancy for flagd and valkey-cart
fix.steps: Deploy a second instance of flagd and place both behind a simple round-robin load balancer (e.g., HAProxy). Replace the single valkey-cart with a Redis master-replica pair using Redis Sentinel for automatic failover. Update service discovery to point to the load balancer and Sentinel endpoints. Test failover by killing each instance individually.
fix.expected_effect: Crashes of flagd or valkey-cart no longer abort the cart journey; the system continues processing with the redundant instance.

traffic+quote.worst_label: combo: spike 100 users + delay quote 50 ms

formula: penalty = 100 x (0.5 x impact + 0.3 x breadth + 0.2 x recovery); service score = 100 - worst penalty on that service; overall = mean of service scores weighted by the number of journeys the service sits on (at least 1; the larger of the map's count and the journeys it was seen to degrade). An experiment whose recovery was not measured (operator stop) contributes no recovery component.
methodology: An independent synthetic prober exercises four user journeys (home, product, cart, checkout) through the front proxy every second. It is the ground truth and does not depend on the application's own telemetry.

A baseline run fixes per-journey error rate and p95 latency and derives safety thresholds from them. A watchdog aborts any experiment that breaches a threshold or loses sight of the prober. Before injection, the safety agent reviews the plan against the baseline limits, recent outcomes and the learned limits, and may approve it, reduce its intensity or veto it; it can never raise an intensity. The planner remembers, across runs, the lowest intensity per target and fault kind that the watchdog or safety agent aborted, and does not propose that intensity or a higher one again within the lookback window. An advisory safety agent re-checks the live measurements every few seconds and may abort earlier; it can never cancel a watchdog abort, extend a fault or change a threshold.

Each experiment injects one fault (container crash, added network delay, packet loss or a traffic spike), measures every journey during the fault window (up to the abort for aborted runs), reverts the fault, and measures how long the journeys take to return inside the baseline band.

A declared combined failure injects 2 faults together as one experiment (one ledger entry per part, one watchdog, one safety review). Every journey limit is tightened for it: p95 limit x0.8, error-rate limit x0.8. It is scored once, as a whole.

Impact, breadth, recovery and the penalty are computed deterministically from those measurements. The hypothesis verdict compares the journeys the planner predicted would degrade with those that actually did: CONFIRMED when equal, PARTIAL when they overlap, REFUTED when they do not.
A hidden dependency is a journey that degraded by at least 0.3 although neither the hypothesis nor the dependency map expected it.

The analyst agent ranks weaknesses and the fixer agent proposes fixes from the measured results only; their output is validated against known experiments, services and an allowlist of compose keys. When Groq is unavailable or its output is invalid, rule-based fallbacks produce the same sections. Fixes are proposals; only restart-policy and raised memory or CPU limit fixes on one allowlisted service can be applied, by `faultline fix`, and are kept only if a re-run of the same experiment improves the penalty.
